The retrieved evidence presents conflicting opinions: d1, d2, d3, and d4 strongly support that chickens can live without their heads, citing the anatomical explanation and the specific case of Miracle Mike surviving 18 months [d1][d2][d3][d4]. d5 offers a hedged version, stating chickens can live a short time but are technically dead [d5]. d6 directly contradicts these by stating no creature can live without its head and that Mike’s brain remained intact, thus he wasn’t truly headless [d6]. This is a conflict of opinions/research outcomes about the possibility and definition of “living without a head.”

Based on the conflicting evidence, the answer must acknowledge the differing perspectives. The majority of documents describe the phenomenon as possible under specific conditions, while one authoritative source disputes it by redefining the case.

Yes, under very specific circumstances a chicken can live without its head, as documented with Miracle Mike who survived 18 months after a beheading that left part of his brain intact [d1][d2][d3][d4]. This occurs because the chicken’s brain anatomy allows the brain stem and cerebellum to remain if the cut is below the eyes [d1]. However, some sources argue that a chicken cannot truly live without its head because essential brain functions must remain, and cases like Mike are not fully headless [d5][d6].
